messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: GPU capacity_exhaustion detected for pool `eu-west-1-gpu-pool` (autoscales failing). High queue growth and throttled requests. Pager triggered at 1765432100. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1765432100 :rotating_light:

Sara L.: seeing queue jump from ~14k to 112k in ~6m. CPU/GPU utilization at 99% for the pool. Autoscaler logs show repeated errors: `scale request rejected: quota/api-rate-limit` and then `scaleup backoff`.

Tom R.: confirmed. metrics: `queue_len_by_priority` shows surge on priority=standard and low. High-priority customers still getting through but 5xx rate is climbing for standard.

Mike (oncall): paging in. I'm attaching the quick-run mitigations from the capacity playbook. If autoscaler can't allocate, we'll need to: 1) throttle low-priority traffic, 2) shift some routes to fallback model variant, 3) open temporary dedicated burst if policy allows.

James K.: logs from autoscaler: 
```
2026-01-14T10:31:27Z ERROR scale_request: 429 QuotaExceeded
2026-01-14T10:31:28Z WARN backoff: next_attempt_in=120s
2026-01-14T10:31:49Z ERROR scale_request: 429 QuotaExceeded
```
We're getting quota hits from the cloud provider on instance creation. That explains partial failures.

Sara L.: estimated customer impact: ~7% of active requests are returning 503s, mostly long-run batching jobs from a few high-volume customers and many small fanout calls. CS has been pinged.

Amy C. (CS): we got a ticket from AcmeCorp reporting degraded response times and intermittent 503s starting ~10:30 UTC. I'll flag the top affected tenants and chase SLAs. Do we need to open an incident customer comms?

Mike (oncall): yes, small comms to affected customers would be good. For immediate mitigation I'm going to: (A) enable autoscale override to temporarily increase max_instances, (B) instruct routing to send `priority=low` to fallback `small-quantized` model, (C) enable enqueue-throttling for non-authenticated API keys.

Tom R.: note that autoscale override attempts also hit the cloud quota. If we can't get new instances we must reduce demand. I can apply routing policy change now.

Tom R.: applying routing policy change for low priority routes to `model:rw-small-q4` -> now. (runbook snippet used)
```
POST /api/v1/routing/update
payload: {"match": "priority=low", "target": "rw-small-q4", "weight": 1.0}
```

Sara L.: started removing non-critical background jobs from the queue (batch replays, analytics ingestion). That dropped queue by ~18k within 6m.

Mike (oncall): applying enqueue-throttle for anonymous keys. Command: `redwoodctl throttles set --pool eu-west-1 --match 'auth=none' --rate 5rps`

Tom R.: throttles applied. Monitor shows queue growth slowing. 503 rate reduced from 7% -> 3.1% in 8m.

James K.: cloud provider support ticket created (SR-987654) citing quota exhaustion for `nvidia-a100` family. ETA unknown; provider suggests request for quota increase but that takes ~hours.

Olivia P.: taking handoff in 30m (leaving in ~25m). What else should I watch?

Mike (oncall): handoff checklist for Olivia: 
- current mitigations in place: low-priority routing -> rw-small-q4, anonymous throttles, background batch pause
- active runbook: `capacity-exhaustion-v2` (link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/capacity-exhaustion-v2)
- key metrics to monitor: `queue_len`, `5xx_rate`, `pool_gpu_util`, `scale_attempt_errors`
- provider SR: SR-987654 (owner: James K.)
- CS comms: Amy C. is drafting a message to affected customers
- next escalation: open cloud provider escalation if SR remains unanswered after 30m or if 5xx>5% for >15m

Olivia P.: ack. I'll monitor and standby for manual burst if provider unblocks. I'll also prepare a canary rollback plan for the routing change in case quality drops on the fallback model.

Amy C. (CS): draft comms posted in #customer-comm-channel for review. Proposed: short note acknowledging degraded performance, mitigation steps, and ETA for fix.

Sara L.: observing slight model-quality alerts for a subset of requests moved to `rw-small-q4`. We'll hold routing weight steady and watch for quality regressions.

Tom R.: provider escalated the SR to quota team; they acknowledged and are expediting. No ETA yet.

Mike (oncall): summary of live mitigations completed: 
- paused non-critical jobs (Sara)
- applied low-priority routing to quantized small variant (Tom)
- enabled anonymous key throttles (Mike)
- CS comms drafted (Amy)
- provider SR opened and escalated (James)

Mike (oncall): action items (owners): 
- James K.: follow provider SR until quota allocation or clear ETA (owner)
- Tom R.: monitor fallbacks and rollback plan if quality drop > 2x baseline (owner)
- Sara L.: run post-incident sweep to confirm no data loss from paused jobs (owner)
- Amy C.: send initial customer comms and update when resolved (owner)
- Olivia P.: take overnight watch and own the incident timeline (owner)

Olivia P.: accepted handoff. I'll post a status update at top of hour and escalate if 5xx>4% persists after 20m.

incident-bot: NOTE: escalation timer set for 20m. If 5xx_rate > 4% at 1765433300, auto-pager to oncall-sre.

Tom R.: small update: 5xx is stable ~2.6%, queue trending down. Still can't scale because cloud quota.

James K.: provider popped a message: they can grant temporary burst of +4 A100s in ~45m if we accept limited region failover. Requesting approval to accept cross-region instances as temporary.

Mike (oncall): approve cross-region burst if it reduces customer impact. Are there ICP/PCI concerns?

Amy C. (CS): cross-region might be fine for non-sensitive tenants; we need to filter by customer tag. I'll produce a list of tagged customers that require geo-restrictions in 10m.

Olivia P.: I'll keep the routing in place and prepare rollback if needed. If provider offers burst, coordinate with infra to ensure networking and routing update.

Tom R.: NOTE: after accepting the temporary cross-region, we should trigger a controlled ingress shift for a small percentage (5%) first to validate.

Mike (oncall): agreed. Waiting on provider SR update. For postmortem: we should evaluate autoscaler backoff policy, cloud quota detection and early circuit (fail-fast to demand reduction), and runbook clarity on cross-region bursts.

Olivia P.: logging a quick summary for night shift: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1765432100/summary (will update)

Amy C. (CS): sending initial customer notice now. Template used and tenant list attached.

Tom R.: current state @ 1765438200: queue 18k (was 112k), 5xx ~1.4%, pool_gpu_util 78%. Keeping mitigations active until provider confirms quota increase or we get stable headroom.

Mike (oncall): closing active pager for now — incident downgraded to priority-2 with night watch. Handing to Olivia. Thanks everyone for quick actions.

Olivia P.: ack. I'll take ownership. Please DM if anything urgent.

Sara L.: +1. Will start the post-incident writeup tomorrow and include timelines, metric graphs, and suggested automation for early demand-shedding triggers.

James K.: keeping SR open. Will post final provider update in this thread when received.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: downgraded to P2 and ownership transferred to Olivia P. at 1765438200.
